test_title: PYST 8: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a principle of Jainism?

options.text: The whole world, including stone and water, has life.
Rejection of the doctrine of Karma
Practice of non-injury to living beings
Monastic life is the only way to salvation.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rejection of the doctrine of Karma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **doctrine of Karma** is a fundamental principle in Jainism that teaches the relationship between a person's actions and their consequences.
 
• In Jain philosophy, Karma is considered a **subtle matter** that binds the soul due to one's actions, thoughts, and desires.
 
• Jainism emphasizes the importance of **liberating the soul** from the bondage of Karma through ethical behavior, self-discipline, and spiritual practices.
 
• The rejection of the doctrine of Karma is not consistent with Jain principles, as Karma serves as the foundation for understanding the cycle of **birth, death, and rebirth (Samsara).**
 
• Jainism encourages individuals to practice **right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct** to overcome the effects of Karma and attain liberation (Moksha).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The whole world, including stone and water, has life**__

 __
 
• Jainism teaches the concept of **Universal Consciousness**, which states that every entity, animate or inanimate, possesses some form of life or soul.
 
• Even elements like stone and water are believed to have souls according to Jain cosmology.
 
• This principle highlights Jainism's emphasis on **respect for all forms of life** and its strict practice of non-violence (Ahimsa).
 
 
 
• **Practice of non-injury to living beings**__
 __
 
• This principle is referred to as **Ahimsa**, which is central to Jain ethical conduct.
 
• Jains avoid causing harm to any living being, whether through thought, speech, or action.
 
• Ahimsa influences dietary practices, professions, and daily activities to ensure minimal harm to other life forms.
 
 
 
• **Monastic life is the only way to salvation**__
 
 
• In Jainism, monastic life is considered the most effective path to achieve **liberation (Moksha).**
 
• Monks and nuns follow strict rules of conduct, renouncing worldly attachments and practicing severe austerities.
 
• However, laypersons can also progress spiritually by following Jain principles and accumulating **positive Karma.**
